references.text: Here Aaron's sons are mentioned: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, the same ones who are named in Exodus 28:1 to serve as priests.
Moses is commanded to take Aaron and his sons to consecrate them for priestly service, fulfilling the command given in Exodus 28:1.
Nadab and Abihu, two of Aaron's sons mentioned in Exodus 28:1, offered unauthorized fire before the Lord and died.
The names of Aaron's sons are listed: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, and their fate as priests is described.
Aaron and his sons are given responsibility for priestly service at the sanctuary, an elaboration on the calling in Exodus 28:1.
The genealogy of Aaron through Eleazar is listed, showing the line of descent from the priestly call in Exodus 28:1.
The anointing oil that ran down upon Aaron's beard and his garments refers to his consecration as high priest.
Hebrews explains that every high priest is chosen from among people and appointed to serve God, just as Aaron was called in Exodus 28:1.
The Levitical priesthood, which began with Aaron, is compared to Christ's priesthood according to the order of Melchizedek.
The selection of priests (28:1) is completed and made concrete through the consecration ritual in the same chapter (28:41).
Anointing at the altar (30:30) is the necessary act to sanctify those chosen as mentioned in 28:1.
Numbers 26:60 confirms historically that the lineage mentioned in Exodus 28:1 continued until the census.
Numbers 3:2 confirms the names and order (firstborn) of the sons who were to perform the service.
The command for consecration in 28:1 is historically fulfilled when the tabernacle is set up in 40:13.
Chronicles shows how the original priests mentioned in 28:1 were organized into divisions.
